newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court reduces fines against West Africa shipping lines.
newsitem.headline: Court reduces fines against West Africa shipping lines.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance reduced but did not annul on Tuesday fines for anti-competitive behavior against maritime transport companies operating between West Africa and Europe.

Compagnie Maritime Belge (CMB), Dafra Lines, Deutsche Afrika-Line and Nedlloyd Line operate a shipping conference between the ports of Zaire and North Sea ports, with the exception of the United Kingdom.

In December 1992, the European Commission fined the four companies 10.1 million Ecus. The major part of the fine, 9.6 million Ecus, was levied against CMB, a group includes Dafra and Deutsche Afrika-Lines.

Refusing to remove the fines outright, the court rejected a series of arguments put forth by the shippers that the Commission acted outside the law, that the shippers did not abuse a dominant position, that a shipping conference should be exempted from competition rules, and that the market concerned was outside of the Commission's jurisdiction.

The court explained that CMB took the largest fine because it played the leading role in the anti-competitive practices, a factor considered more relevant by the court than CMB's share in the conference earning's pool.
The court reduced the total amount of fines by almost 1 million Ecus, noting, inter alia, the period taken into consideration by the Commission was too long.
(Court translation into English. Original languages of the joined cases: German, English and Dutch)
